Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary here and we'll follow up with engineers/legal for artifacts.

- High level: deletion is a two-step process: a tombstone (logical delete) is created immediately; physical expunge runs during scheduled GC sweeps. Default retention for user-facing snapshots is 30 days, after which tombstones are eligible for sweep.
- Cross-region: replication is asynchronous. Typical replication completes within 6–24 hours depending on region, but expunge propagation to replicated offsite snapshots depends on both replication lag and the next GC window — worst case we advise to assume 72 hours after tombstone eligibility for cross-region expunge.
- KMS: destroying a customer-managed key will render ciphertext irrecoverable, but Redwood will not perform irreversible key destruction on behalf of customers without explicit BYOK key deletion requests and extra safeguards. KMS destruction is not a substitute for documented expunge in our records; we can provide key lifecycle logs if you need them.
- Legal hold: legal/retention holds will suspend GC sweep for the affected objects; we record hold state in the audit log and can generate evidence showing the hold ID, start/end times, and impacted artifacts.

I'll loop in Karthik for the deeper technical flow and Marissa for the attestation language. We can produce the policy PDF and a flow diagram — attaching the current policy doc for your review.

On Sat, 11 Oct 2026 at 10:05 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:

Jordan / Sarah — adding technical detail on the expunge mechanics and timings.

1) Tombstones & sweep windows: After a delete, we mark objects with a tombstone and place them in a per-region tombstone index. A region-local GC sweep runs every 12 hours by default; we also have a global coordinated purge for cross-region cleanup that runs every 24 hours. An object becomes eligible for physical removal after the configured retention TTL expires (default 30d) + any active holds.

2) Replication semantics: Snapshot replication is async (log shipping + periodic checkpoint). If a snapshot was replicated before the tombstone was created, the replica will retain the data until that replica's local GC processes the tombstone; because of the async window you should assume up to an additional 48 hours beyond local sweep windows in worst-case cross-region scenarios (network outages, backlog).

3) Key handling: For Redwood-managed KMS, we maintain key rotation and soft-deactivation prior to destruction. Even after key destruction, we keep audit entries showing key id, destruction request time, and the set of encrypted objects affected. For BYOK, customers control key lifecycle — destroying the key in a BYOK flow makes the data unrecoverable, but Redwood will still show tombstone and expunge events. Note: for regulated customers we recommend a documented key-destruct workflow and signed attestation.

4) Evidence and logs: We can export an expunge trace for a given object id (timestamps for tombstone creation, GC sweep, cross-region acknowledgement) and provide S3/Drive-stored CSV logs or a signed PDF summary.

I'll attach an expunge flow diagram and a sample trace export if useful. Happy to schedule a quick sync to walk through an example object.
